item.title: Iran’s Real War Is Against the Global Economy
item.description: EST President Navin Girishankar argues that Iran may be losing the military contest with the United States, but it is fighting a different war—one aimed at the global economy.

item.title: What Is at Stake in Hungary’s Election?
item.description: Hungary’s April election could end Viktor Orbán’s 16-year rule as opposition leader Peter Magyar mounts a serious challenge. The outcome will shape Hungary’s democratic trajectory and impact the European Union’s unity and policy for years to come.

item.title: Unpacking Iran’s Drone Campaign in the Gulf: Early Lessons for Future Drone Warfare
item.description: Kateryna Bondar analyzes Iran’s drone retaliation campaign during Operation Epic Fury, showing how mass one-way attack drones are reshaping air warfare and what lessons the United States can draw from both the Gulf conflict and Ukraine’s experience.

item.title: Chicken Soup Coming Home to Roost
item.description: This week, Bill Reinsch analyzes the impact of the Trump administration’s steel tariffs, highlighting how they have raised the cost of goods and added complexity to compliance efforts.

item.title: What Does the New Cyber Strategy Really Mean?
item.description: The new U.S. cyber strategy marks a shift to a more proactive cyber policy. It is a commendable declaration of goals but lacks a conversation about matching resources to these goals. This analysis explores the strategy’s strengths, gaps, and the path forward.
